observation: The whole set in the opening position, and it is coherent. Iso: a 7 by 9 grey field in four panels with a grid cut into it, sixteen worlds each standing on its own cell centre, twelve cocoa asteroid tiles in two blocks of six across the middle ranks, a star at each end with two flames off the board edge and three sunken corona cells round each, and the two trays parked clear of the far edge. Top: every piece is concentric with its cell and nothing overlaps a grid line, a tile edge or another piece; the trays are wholly off the board. Front: the rank ladder is visible and monotone -- Mercury is the smallest ball and Jupiter the largest, and Saturn is the second largest and the only one wearing a ring. The two armies read as mirrors: white discs facing black ones, and each pair of worlds leaning its pole the opposite way. Saturn's Sol and Anti-Sol pieces lean their rings in opposite directions, which is the ownership cue doing its job. Nothing is missing, nothing is duplicated, nothing floats, and there is no visible intersection anywhere -- no piece into a tile, no flame into a piece, no tray into the board. Two renderer properties rather than geometry, both already on the record: a black Anti-Sol disc reads as a featureless silhouette because the shading is flat with no ground plane, and the seven-segment numerals on the disc walls face the two seated players so they are edge-on at this camera.
